## Summary

Replace the per-definition `skip_rocm_test: bool` on integration tests with a
per-backend `skip_cases.toml`:

- one section per backend, matched against `utils.device_type`; `all` applies to
  every backend, and `cuda` / `rocm` are distinguished with
  `torch.version.hip`;
- the loader merges every source into one skip table; the runner filters during
  selection and logs the matched section;
- out-of-tree devices can register their own TOML through an entry point or by
  calling `register_skip_cases()` explicitly, using the same format and parser
  as the in-tree file;
- the default rules migrate the 24 ROCm skips in the core suites; the seven
  graph_trainer skips move to their own TOML, registered by that runner with
  `suites=`;
- add a README, a rule, and unit tests.

## Background

Integration tests currently have no unified skip mechanism: skipping is spread
across per-definition booleans, and some of them, such as skip_rocm_test, are
tightly coupled to specific hardware.

## Design

Skip rules live under `tests/integration_tests/skips/`:

```text
tests/integration_tests/skips/
  __init__.py        # parse, merge, validate, query
  skip_cases.toml    # default rules maintained by titan
  README.md          # format and registration
```

### TOML format

```toml
[rocm]
features = [
  "sdc_replay_accelerator_graph",
  "fsdp_pp_deferred_gradient_reduction",
]
models = [
  "deepseek_v3_fused_mla_swiglu_fsdp+ep",
  "qwen3_5_moe_fsdp+tp+ep",
]
h100 = [
  "dist_gemm",   # symmetric memory is CUDA-only
]
```

- section names are matched against the backend: `npu` / `xpu` and so on compare
  directly with `utils.device_type`; `cuda` and `rocm` are special cases because
  both report `device_type == "cuda"`, and are distinguished with
  `torch.version.hip`; `all` applies to every backend;
- keys are suite names, defaulting to the `_TEST_SUITES` values in
  `tests/integration_tests/run_tests.py`; a registered file can extend them with
  `suites=`;
- values are the `test_name`s of that suite's `IntegrationTestDefinition`
  entries;
- reasons are trailing comments on the entry; a suite or test-name mismatch
  raises `ValueError` before any test starts.

### Registering an out-of-tree device

Beyond the default file, an out-of-tree device can register its own TOML, using
the same schema, in two ways:

1. entry point:

   ```toml
   [project.entry-points."torchtitan.skip_cases"]
   device = "your_package.skips:register"
   ```

   ```python
   # your_package/skips/__init__.py
   def register(): register_skip_cases("path/to/your_toml")
   ```

   Set `TORCHTITAN_SKIP_CASES_AUTOLOAD=0` to disable automatic registration.

2. call `register_skip_cases(path)` directly from the test bootstrap.

In both cases `suites=` can be omitted; the file is then held to titan's own
suite list. Pass it only when the file introduces suites outside `_TEST_SUITES`.

## Migration

- remove `skip_rocm_test` from `IntegrationTestDefinition`;
- move the 24 `skip_rocm_test=True` entries in the core suites into `[rocm]`;
- move the seven graph_trainer `skip_rocm_test=True` entries into
  `torchtitan/experiments/graph_trainer/tests/skips/skip_cases.toml`, registered
  by that runner with `suites=set(_TEST_SUITES_FUNCTION)`;
- add `tests/integration_tests/skips/README.md`, link it from the Test Structure
  in `tests/README.md`, and add a rule to `.claude/rules/tests.md`;
- the test cases themselves are unchanged; out-of-tree callers that still pass
  `skip_rocm_test` are incompatible and need to move to the TOML.

## Validation

Selection over the current main inventory (86 definitions: features 51 /
models 26 / h100 9):

- CUDA: 86 runnable / 0 filtered;
- ROCm: 62 runnable / 24 filtered (features 14 / models 6 / h100 4), matching the
  current `skip_rocm_test=True` count;
- `tests/unit_tests/cpu/test_skip_cases.py`: 5 tests pass, covering
  parse/validation errors, suite declaration, section matching, entry-point
  registration/failure, and the no-`test_suite` runner.

This adds three extension mechanisms: the `torchtitan.skip_cases` entry-point group, the `register_skip_cases()` API, and two env vars (`TORCHTITAN_SKIP_CASES`, `TORCHTITAN_SKIP_CASES_AUTOLOAD`). None of them has an in-repo consumer or a named out-of-tree user. `.claude/rules/design.md` says not to build plugin systems or registries before a second implementation exists, and to keep env vars to a minimum.

Out-of-tree CI can already skip tests without any of this: `--exclude name1,name2` (`run_tests.py:588`). If a device repo needs more than that, please name the user and say why `--exclude` doesn't work for them.

Separately, lines 100-104 read files, read env vars and run third-party entry points when the module is imported. `design.md` asks that imports have no side effects.

## Summary

Replace the per-definition `skip_rocm_test: bool` on integration tests with a
per-backend `skip_cases.toml`:

- one section per backend, matched against `utils.device_type`; `all` applies to
  every backend, and `cuda` / `rocm` are distinguished with
  `torch.version.hip`;
- the loader merges every source into one skip table; the runner filters during
  selection and logs the matched section;
- out-of-tree devices can register their own TOML through an entry point or by
  calling `register_skip_cases()` explicitly, using the same format and parser
  as the in-tree file;
- the default rules migrate the 24 ROCm skips in the core suites; the seven
  graph_trainer skips move to their own TOML, registered by that runner with
  `suites=`;
- add a README, a rule, and unit tests.

## Background

Integration tests currently have no unified skip mechanism: skipping is spread
across per-definition booleans, and some of them, such as skip_rocm_test, are
tightly coupled to specific hardware.

## Design

Skip rules live under `tests/integration_tests/skips/`:

```text
tests/integration_tests/skips/
  __init__.py        # parse, merge, validate, query
  skip_cases.toml    # default rules maintained by titan
  README.md          # format and registration
```

### TOML format

```toml
[rocm]
features = [
  "sdc_replay_accelerator_graph",
  "fsdp_pp_deferred_gradient_reduction",
]
models = [
```

- section names are matched against the backend: `npu` / `xpu` and so on compare
  directly with `utils.device_type`; `cuda` and `rocm` are special cases because
  both report `device_type == "cuda"`, and are distinguished with
  `torch.version.hip`; `all` applies to every backend;
- keys are suite names, defaulting to the `_TEST_SUITES` values in
  `tests/integration_tests/run_tests.py`; a registered file can extend them with
  `suites=`;
- values are the `test_name`s of that suite's `IntegrationTestDefinition`
  entries;
- reasons are trailing comments on the entry; a suite or test-name mismatch
  raises `ValueError` before any test starts.

### Registering an out-of-tree device

Beyond the default file, an out-of-tree device can register its own TOML, using
the same schema, in two ways:

1. entry point:

   ```toml
   [project.entry-points."torchtitan.skip_cases"]
   device = "your_package.skips:register"
   ```

   ```python
   def register(): register_skip_cases("path/to/your_toml")
   ```

2. call `register_skip_cases(path)` directly from the test bootstrap.

In both cases `suites=` can be omitted; the file is then held to titan's own
suite list. Pass it only when the file introduces suites outside `_TEST_SUITES`.

- remove `skip_rocm_test` from `IntegrationTestDefinition`;
- move the 24 `skip_rocm_test=True` entries in the core suites into `[rocm]`;
- move the seven graph_trainer `skip_rocm_test=True` entries into
  `torchtitan/experiments/graph_trainer/tests/skips/skip_cases.toml`, registered
  by that runner with `suites=set(_TEST_SUITES_FUNCTION)`;
- add `tests/integration_tests/skips/README.md`, link it from the Test Structure
  in `tests/README.md`, and add a rule to `.claude/rules/tests.md`;
- the test cases themselves are unchanged; out-of-tree callers that still pass
  `skip_rocm_test` are incompatible and need to move to the TOML.

## Validation

Selection over the current main inventory (86 definitions: features 51 /
models 26 / h100 9):

- CUDA: 86 runnable / 0 filtered;
- ROCm: 62 runnable / 24 filtered (features 14 / models 6 / h100 4), matching the
  current `skip_rocm_test=True` count;
- `tests/unit_tests/cpu/test_skip_cases.py`: 5 tests pass, covering
  parse/validation errors, suite declaration, section matching, entry-point
  registration/failure, and the no-`test_suite` runner.

+# Integration test skips
+
+`skip_cases.toml` in this directory lists integration tests that must not run on
+a given backend. `tests/integration_tests/run_tests.py` reads it from
+`_filter_tests`: a matching test is dropped before anything is launched, and the
+skip is logged with the section that matched.
+
+## File format
+
+One section per backend, one key per suite, one array of test names:
+
+```toml
+[rocm]
+features = [
+  "sdc_replay_accelerator_graph",
+  "fsdp_pp_deferred_gradient_reduction",
+]
+models = [
+  "deepseek_v3_fused_mla_swiglu_fsdp+ep",
+  "qwen3_5_moe_fsdp+tp+ep",
+]
+h100 = [
+  "dist_gemm",   # symmetric memory is CUDA-only
+]
+```
+
+- A section name aligns with `utils.device_type` (for example `xpu`). `all`,
+  `cuda`, and `rocm` are special cases: `all` applies to every backend, and
+  because ROCm also reports `device_type == "cuda"`, `cuda` and `rocm` are
+  distinguished with `torch.version.hip`.
+- Keys are suite names. By default they are the `_TEST_SUITES` values of
+  `tests/integration_tests/run_tests.py`; a registered file can extend them with
+  `suites=`.
+- Values are `test_name`s of that suite's `IntegrationTestDefinition` entries.
+- Reasons are trailing comments on the entry; an entry without a comment is
+  fine.
+- Suite names are checked against the suites the file may name, and test names
+  against the suite being run; either mismatch raises `ValueError` before any
+  test starts.
+
+## Registering skips from an out-of-tree device repo
+
+A device repo ships its own file with the same schema and registers it. Two
+ways, in order of preference:
+
+### 1. Entry point (automatic)
+
+```toml
+# pyproject.toml of the device repo
+[project.entry-points."torchtitan.skip_cases"]
+my_device = "my_device.tests:register_skips"
+```
+
+```python
+# my_device/tests.py
+from tests.integration_tests.skips import register_skip_cases
+
+
+def register_skips() -> None:
+    register_skip_cases("path/to/your_toml")
+```
+
+Set `TORCHTITAN_SKIP_CASES_AUTOLOAD=0` to disable automatic registration.
+
+### 2. Explicit call
+
+Call `register_skip_cases(path)` from the device repo before its runner calls
+`run_tests()`, i.e. before the test list is filtered.
+
+In both cases `suites=` can be omitted; the file is then held to titan's own
+suites. Pass it only when the file introduces new suites, for example when an
+experiment registers suites that are not in `_TEST_SUITES`:
+
+```python
+register_skip_cases(path, suites={"my_suite"})
+```
+
+Both ways use the same parser and the same section/suite schema, so a device
+file behaves exactly like the in-tree one.
+
+## Where a skip belongs
+
+| Mechanism | Use for | Lives in |
+|---|---|---|
+| `skip_cases.toml` | permanent, backend-wide skips | this directory |
+| `disabled=True` | skips not caused by hardware coupling, and temporary one-off skips | the definition |
+| `--exclude a,b,c` | skipping a few cases for one invocation | the command line |

+"""Skip cases for integration tests.
+
+The default rules live in ``skip_cases.toml`` next to this module. A hardware
+backend can register an additional file in two ways:
+
+* an entry point in the ``torchtitan.skip_cases`` group, loaded automatically
+  and disabled with ``TORCHTITAN_SKIP_CASES_AUTOLOAD=0``;
+* :func:`register_skip_cases`, called from a test bootstrap.
+
+All files use the same schema and are merged into one set of sections.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import logging
+import os
+import tomllib
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+from pathlib import Path
+from typing import Collection, Mapping
+
+import torch
+
+from torchtitan.tools import utils
+
+logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
+
+SKIP_CASES_FILE = Path(__file__).with_name("skip_cases.toml")
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class SkipSection:
+    name: str
+    skips: Mapping[str, frozenset[str]]
+    source: str
+
+
+def _parse(text: str, source: str) -> list[SkipSection]:
+    raw = tomllib.loads(text)
+    sections: list[SkipSection] = []
+    for name, cfg in raw.items():
+        if not isinstance(cfg, dict):
+            raise ValueError(f"{source}: section {name!r} must be a table")
+        skips: dict[str, frozenset[str]] = {}
+        for suite, tests in cfg.items():
+            if not isinstance(tests, list) or not all(
+                isinstance(test, str) for test in tests
+            ):
+                raise ValueError(
+                    f"{source}: {name}.{suite} must be an array of strings"
+                )
+            skips[suite] = frozenset(tests)
+        sections.append(SkipSection(name, skips, source))
+    return sections
+
+
+_SECTIONS: list[SkipSection] = []
+# Suites an outside file may name: the default file is held to the core suites
+# of tests/integration_tests/run_tests.py, while a file registered with
+# ``suites=`` declares its own.
+_OUTSIDE_SUITES: dict[str, frozenset[str]] = {}
+
+
+def register_skip_cases(
+    source: str | Path, *, suites: Collection[str] | None = None
+) -> None:
+    """Register an additional skip-cases file with the same schema.
+
+    ``suites`` declares the suite names the file may mention; without it the
+    file is held to the core suites of ``tests.integration_tests.run_tests``.
+    Registration must happen before the runner starts filtering tests.
+    """
+    _load()
+    path = Path(source)
+    _SECTIONS.extend(_parse(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"), str(path)))
+    if suites is not None:
+        _OUTSIDE_SUITES[str(path)] = frozenset(suites)
+
+
+def _import_skip_case_extensions() -> None:
+    """Leverage the Python plugin mechanism to load out-of-the-tree skip cases."""
+    from importlib.metadata import entry_points
+
+    group_name = "torchtitan.skip_cases"
+    skip_case_extensions = entry_points(group=group_name)
+
+    for skip_case_extension in skip_case_extensions:
+        try:
+            entrypoint = skip_case_extension.load()
+            entrypoint()
+        except Exception as err:
+            raise RuntimeError(
+                f"Failed to load the skip-cases extension: "
+                f"{skip_case_extension.name}. You can disable extension "
+                "auto-loading with TORCHTITAN_SKIP_CASES_AUTOLOAD=0."
+            ) from err
+
+
+def _is_skip_case_autoload_enabled() -> bool:
+    return os.getenv("TORCHTITAN_SKIP_CASES_AUTOLOAD", "1") == "1"
+
+
+_loaded = False
+_loading = False
+
+
+def _load() -> None:
+    """Read the default file and the entry points.
+
+    Runs on first use instead of at import, so importing this module reads
+    no files and executes no third-party code.
+    """
+    global _loaded, _loading
+    if _loaded or _loading:
+        return
+    # ``_loading`` covers re-entry (an entry point may call register_skip_cases);
+    # ``_loaded`` is only set once everything was read, so a malformed file
+    # leaves the state empty instead of half-filled.
+    _loading = True
+    try:
+        _SECTIONS.extend(
+            _parse(SKIP_CASES_FILE.read_text(encoding="utf-8"), str(SKIP_CASES_FILE))
+        )
+        if _is_skip_case_autoload_enabled():
+            _import_skip_case_extensions()
+        _loaded = True
+    finally:
+        _loading = False
+
+
+def _section_applies(name: str) -> bool:
+    if name == "all":
+        return True
+    if name == "rocm":
+        return utils.device_type == "cuda" and torch.version.hip is not None
+    if name == "cuda":
+        return utils.device_type == "cuda" and torch.version.hip is None
+    return utils.device_type == name
+
+
+def validate_suite(
+    suite: str | None, known: set[str], core_suites: Collection[str]
+) -> None:
+    """Reject entries that reference unknown suites or test names.
+
+    ``core_suites`` are the suites the default file may name. A registered file
+    may declare its own suites via ``register_skip_cases(..., suites=...)``;
+    without a declaration it is held to the same list. Test names are only
+    checked for ``suite``, the one being run.
+    """
+    _load()
+    allowed_core_suites = set(core_suites)
+    for section in _SECTIONS:
+        unknown_suites = set(section.skips) - _OUTSIDE_SUITES.get(
+            section.source, allowed_core_suites
+        )
+        if unknown_suites:
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"{section.source}: section {section.name!r} references "
+                f"unknown suite(s) {sorted(unknown_suites)}"
+            )
+        if suite is None:
+            continue
+        tests = section.skips.get(suite)
+        if tests is None:
+            continue
+        unknown = tests - known
+        if unknown:
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"{section.source}: section {section.name!r}, suite "
+                f"{suite!r}: unknown test(s) {sorted(unknown)}"
+            )
+
+
+def active_skips() -> dict[tuple[str, str], str]:
+    """Map (suite, test_name) to the section that applies on this machine."""
+    _load()
+    active: dict[tuple[str, str], str] = {}
+    for section in _SECTIONS:
+        if not _section_applies(section.name):
+            continue
+        for suite, tests in section.skips.items():
+            for test_name in tests:
+                active[(suite, test_name)] = section.name
+    return active
